hooks.text: 27 missed calls × $140 = $3,800 in lost revenue
hooks.why_it_works: Specific dollar amount + multiplication = concrete self-application. The reader pauses to check their own numbers. The 27/140/3800 trio is the load-bearing element; abstract claims would lose the reader in 3 lines.

hooks.text: I replaced a $25/hr virtual assistant with AI and I don't feel good about it
hooks.why_it_works: Vulnerability + specific $ figure. The reader either sees themselves or knows someone who does. The 'I don't feel good about it' frame is permission-giving for the small business owner mid-replacement.

hooks.text: 40-60% of revenue-generating calls come outside 9-5, but only 12% get captured
hooks.why_it_works: Data drop with before/after framing. 9-5 is the assumed working window; the stat reframes it as the trap. The gap (40-60% vs 12%) is the AI voice agent pitch in two numbers.

hooks.text: Plumbers lose $15k a month to missed calls
hooks.why_it_works: Monthly framing = 'this is happening right now.' Recurring loss is scarier than one-time. The $15k figure is specific enough to feel real, large enough to demand action.

hooks.text: Voicemail doesn't work
hooks.why_it_works: States the obvious. The reader nods, then is ready for the alternative. Consensus statements are underrated — they lower the buy-in cost for the pitch that follows.

hooks.text: Disk is ground truth. Named projects in a directive are claims, not facts.
hooks.why_it_works: Hard rule, staccato. Recap-vs-disk is the failure mode every LLM agent hits. The reader nods because they've been burned.

hooks.text: If a metric is obscured, write 'unclear.' Never hallucinate a number.
hooks.why_it_works: Hard rule, staccato. The reader either sees themselves fabricating numbers or sees themselves being burned by others' fabrications. The discipline is asymmetric by design.

hooks.text: A single-file state is fine for a chief-sequential system. The instant you need concurrent writers, you need a real lock manager.
hooks.why_it_works: Names the threshold. Engineers love named thresholds. 'Chief-sequential' is jargon that pays off because it pins the design choice.

hooks.text: Atomic write is the load-bearing pattern. Temp-write-fsync-rename. The 3 specs share the same Python code inline.
hooks.why_it_works: Shows the discipline, not just describes it. Engineers want to see code, not principles. The spec-sharing pattern is the load-bearing meta-insight.

hooks.text: When flipping a status in a shared state, match by Python is-identity. Not by text. The text-match race with another rephrased draft is the bug.
hooks.why_it_works: Specific (Python is-identity) + general (the race-condition class). Engineers need both. The 'not by text' negation tells the reader what was tried and failed.

hooks.text: Amazon takes 40% of every dollar before we see it
hooks.why_it_works: Specific dollar amount + 'before we see it' framing. The reader's eyes lock on the margin. The 40% number is conservative (15% referral + 30-40% FBA + ads = 45-55% all-in). The hook understates the bleed to be believable.

hooks.text: We were #1 in the map pack and our calls dropped 40%
hooks.why_it_works: The inverse of expected (#1 = good) + a specific loss. The reader either sees themselves or a competitor. The 40% number is the load-bearing element; abstract 'calls dropped' would lose the reader in 3 lines.

hooks.text: I lost $30k to overselling last quarter
hooks.why_it_works: Specific $ amount + 'last quarter' = recent, recurring. The reader checks their own books. The $30k figure is the size of a small-business payroll or a year's marketing budget — visceral.

hooks.text: A 10K-page template site is outranking me on every long-tail query
hooks.why_it_works: The volume asymmetry is concrete (10K vs 50 pages). The reader's hand goes to the keyboard to check. The pSEO threat is the new local-business problem; this hook names it without preaching.

hooks.text: ChatGPT cited our competitor, not us
hooks.why_it_works: The AI-vs-competitor framing. The reader either sees themselves or their competitors. Specific (ChatGPT, not 'AI' in general) and binary (cited them, didn't cite us). The recognition is the new normal.

formats.structure: Math-Problem Drop: [X units] × [$Y] = $[Z]. [Implication in 1 sentence.]
formats.why_it_works: Single-line math, no commentary, let the numbers hit. The implication sentence is optional. Best for operators who think in $/job, not impressions.

formats.structure: Confession / Vulnerability Post: 'I did X. [Specific $ or stat]. I don't feel good about it. Here's what I learned.'
formats.why_it_works: First-person, specific dollar amount, the discomfort frame. Small business owners want permission to automate but feel weird about it. The confession IS the hook.

formats.structure: Data Drop + Implication: '[Stat 1] vs [Stat 2]. [One-line consequence].'
formats.why_it_works: Two numbers in tension. The reader's eye locks on the gap. The one-line consequence turns the data into a call to action.

formats.structure: Recurring Loss Frame: '$[N per period] lost to [thing]. [The fix in one line].'
formats.why_it_works: Periodic framing is scarier than one-time. The fix in one line is the load-bearing element — proves the operator can act THIS period, not someday.

formats.structure: Consensus Statement + Pivot: '[Obvious thing everyone agrees on]. [What actually works instead].'
formats.why_it_works: Agree first, then redirect. Lowers the buy-in cost. The pivot sentence is where the new product/idea lives.

formats.structure: Discipline Drop: [Hard rule]. [Why it exists]. [What would happen if you didn't have it].
formats.why_it_works: The hard rule lands in the first sentence. The 'why' is the load-bearing element — proves the rule is load-bearing, not arbitrary. The 'what would happen' closes with the cost of breaking it.

formats.structure: Threshold Name: [Design choice X] is fine for [condition Y]. The instant you need [condition Z], you need [alternative W].
formats.why_it_works: Names the threshold. Engineers love named thresholds — gives them a decision rule. The 'instant you need' phrasing is a code trigger; the 'alternative W' is the migration path.

formats.structure: Rule + Counter-Rule: [Hard rule A]. [The failure mode A prevents]. [The trap that looks like A but isn't].
formats.why_it_works: States the rule, then negates the common false-positive. The trap is the load-bearing element — proves the chief has seen it, not just the rule. Engineers trust people who know the trap.

formats.structure: Spec-Sharing Pattern: [N] specs share the same [pattern]. [Why they share it]. [What happens when a N+1 writer joins].
formats.why_it_works: Shows the discipline, not just describes it. The 'N+1 writer' future-proofing is the implicit promise that the system is designed for growth.

formats.structure: What Worked / What Broke / What's Next: [Build]. [Failed at X]. [Recovered by Y]. [The lesson].
formats.why_it_works: The canonical build log. Engineers trust the asymmetric report — what broke is more valuable than what worked. The 'recovered by Y' is the load-bearing element (shows recovery is real, not theoretical).

formats.structure: Margin-Cost Drop: Platform X takes Y% of $Z. [Implication in 1 sentence].
formats.why_it_works: Specific platform + percentage + dollar framing. The 'before we see it' phrase locks the reader on the margin. Pillar 1 default.

formats.structure: Rank-Loss Confession: We were #1 in [place]. [Specific metric dropped by N%]. [What happened next].
formats.why_it_works: The inverse of expected (we were winning) + a specific loss. Pillar 3 default. The 'what happened next' closes with the cause or the recovery.

formats.structure: Specific $ Loss: [N units] × [$Y] = $[Z lost]. [Why it happened].
formats.why_it_works: Multiplication-as-surgery. The reader checks their own numbers. Pillar 1 + Pillar 3 both use this for math-anchored posts.

formats.structure: Volume-Asymmetry Alert: [A] pages outranking [B] pages on [query type].
formats.why_it_works: The asymmetry is concrete (10K vs 50). The reader knows the war is asymmetric before they finish the sentence. Pillar 3 specific — the pSEO threat.

formats.structure: AI-Citation Observation: I asked [AI] about [topic]. [What it cited]. [What I learned].
formats.why_it_works: The first-person observation + specific AI + specific topic. Pillar 3 specific — the GEO discipline. The 'what I learned' closes with the action.

formats.structure: Regulatory Cliff Drop: [Platform] [year] SLA: [threshold 1], [threshold 2], [penalty]. [Merchant math]. [The fix].
formats.why_it_works: Four hard numbers in two sentences. The reader runs their own numbers in real-time. The regulatory framing elevates the stakes from 'tool problem' to 'business survival.' Pillar 1 specific.

formats.structure: Audit Drop + Imperative Close: I audited [N] [category] tools. [Verdict]. [What each one needs]. [The one fix that closes the gap].
formats.why_it_works: The categorical claim (all N are wrappers) earns authority because the audit is specific. The 'what each one needs' section is the content — it shows the author has done the technical work. The imperative close tells the reader exactly what to do next. Pillar 4 / Build Log default.

formats.structure: Vendor-Indictment Drop: [Vendor]'s own [document type] ([date]): '[exact limitation quote].' [Verdict].
formats.why_it_works: Uses the vendor's own words against the vendor. The document date is the load-bearing element — it proves the limitation was known at launch, not discovered post-sale. The reader who has this tool sees their own situation in the quote.

formats.structure: Cost-Quantification Table: [Line item] | Wrapper-tier | True Agent |. [Net delta]. [Payback period].
formats.why_it_works: Side-by-side numbers make the ROI undeniable. The 'wrapper vs True Agent' framing elevates the buyer from 'which tool?' to 'which architecture?' Pillar 2 default for the trades cost math.

formats.structure: Structural Diagnosis + Pivot: [The wrapper claim]. [The system-of-record truth]. [The distinction that changes the build].
formats.why_it_works: Three beats: what the vendor says, why that claim is wrong, and the one conceptual move that fixes it. The 'UI speed vs data truth' distinction is the conceptual pivot. Engineers and operators both trust this structure.

formats.structure: Contrarian-Hype + Operator Implementation: 'Everyone is hyping [X]. Who cares. Here is what [OPERATOR] can do: 1. [step] 2. [step] 3. [step] 4. [step]. Cost: $[N]/mo. Time saved: [N] hr/wk. Boring. Profitable.'
formats.why_it_works: The Pillar 6 dominant format. Contrarian opener + named operator + 4-step recipe + cost-time math + 'Boring. Profitable.' closer. Sources 2, 4, 5 all surface this structure independently.

formats.structure: Leverage Pivot (Fear → Action): 'AI is going to take my job. [Fear acknowledgment]. [The real threat]. Here's the 30-minute fix this weekend.'
formats.why_it_works: Acknowledge the fear in sentence 1. Pivot to the real threat in sentence 2. Give the action in sentence 3. Sources 1 and 4 both use this 3-beat structure. The 30-min anchor is the frictionless entry.

formats.structure: Data + Implication + Action: '[Specific stat] (Source). [What it means for you]. [The specific action].'
formats.why_it_works: GitHub Copilot 55% + less-experienced developers benefit most is the data anchor. The 'what it means' ties it to the reader's identity. The action closes with the specific setup cost ($20/mo) and the weekly time saved.

formats.structure: 5-Question Filter: 'Does it save 1+ hr/week? [Y/N] / Work with tools I already use? [Y/N] / Cost < time-saved × $50/hr? [Y/N] / Install in <4 hrs? [Y/N] / Usage-based pricing? [Y/N]. 4 of 5 = test it.'
formats.why_it_works: Source 3 surfaces this as the decision-discipline pattern. Five binary questions, explicit threshold (4 of 5). The reader can run it Monday morning on the next 3 announcements. The meta-value ('I have a filter') is the brand signal.

formats.structure: Cultural Observation + Implication: 'A new [TOOL] dropped Tuesday. By Wednesday: [N] demos, [N] think-pieces, [N] practical breakdowns. The [N] broke out.'
formats.why_it_works: The meta-commentary pattern. The specific number trio (1,100/90/10) is the load-bearing element. The implication ('the 10 broke out') tells the reader why this matters without preaching. Sources 1 and 5 both surface the speed-to-tactical discipline.

formats.structure: Penalty-vs-Margin Drop: [Per-unit penalty] > [per-unit margin]. [Late rate] × [monthly volume] = $[loss/month]. [The fix in 1 line].
